blocks.text: Heritage Mountain: streets and boundaries

items.t: Heritage Mountain is a City of Port Moody neighbourhood grouping, not a separate municipality: Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw, 2026, No.

The street pattern is the point here: Ravine Drive, Noons Creek Drive and Turner Creek Drive climb off Heritage Mountain Boulevard, and David Avenue is the east-west exit toward Ioco Road or Coquitlam.
The north edge is forest, not houses: Bert Flinn Park backs the upper streets, and the Village of Anmore sits beyond the city boundary on East Road.

blocks.text: Heritage Mountain: the housing stock

items.t: Two named pockets sit inside this side of the grouping: Twin Creeks and Noons Creek, both around Noons Creek Drive, separate in local use from Heritage Woods east of Forest Park Way.

blocks.text: Heritage Mountain: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Heritage Mountain Elementary at 125 Ravine Drive sits inside the neighbourhood; the secondary building buyers picture, Heritage Woods Secondary at 1300 David Avenue, is in Heritage Woods, not here.
There is no library branch in Heritage Mountain; the single Port Moody Public Library is at 100 Newport Drive in Inlet Centre.
Port Moody was declared a Bear Smart Community in 2024, and landscaping beside sensitive areas here must use the City Preferred Plant List with bear-resistant waste enclosures.

blocks.text: Heritage Mountain: getting around

items.t: Route 182 is the through-route: Moody Centre Station/Belcarra, crossing Heritage Mountain on Ravine Drive and Turner Creek Drive before David Avenue.

blocks.text: Heritage Mountain home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

19 houses sold in Heritage Mountain with a median price of $1,750,000 (the middle half sold between $1,676,500 and $2,070,000), taking a median of 14 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 11% sold above list. They had a median $460 per square foot, a median year built of 1992 and a median lot of 6,543 square feet. 11 townhomes sold in Heritage Mountain with a median price of $1,320,000 (the middle half sold between $1,217,500 and $1,344,500), taking a median of 13 days to sell at 98.2% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $541 per square foot, a median year built of 1991 and a median strata fee of $581 a month.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Heritage Mountain?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 11 houses and 4 condos and townhomes listed in Heritage Mountain. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Heritage Mountain a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes had 25% on only 4 listed, too few to read as a market type. The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Heritage Mountain from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 10 houses and 7 condos and townhomes sold in Heritage Mountain over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in July with 4 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in July with 3 sold.

faq.q: How big is Heritage Mountain compared with the rest of Port Moody?
faq.a: In October 2026, Heritage Mountain held 8.0% of the 138 detached houses listed in Port Moody and 2.4% of the 168 condos and townhomes listed in Port Moody.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Heritage Mountain?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 73.3% of the 15 homes listed in Heritage Mountain and condos and townhomes made up 26.7%; of the 1 that sold, houses were 0.0% and condos and townhomes 100.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Heritage Mountain than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was little changed, 11 in June and 11 in October 2026 (+0.0%); condos and townhomes fell from 9 in June to 4 in October 2026 (−55.6%).

Only in part. Dogs may be off leash at any time on Bert Flinn Park's wide gravel trail, and from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m. only on the Morning Off-Leash Mini Loop, a one-year pilot the City is monitoring through late 2026; everywhere else in the park is on-leash, and non-compliance can draw a ticket under Bylaw No. 3343.

faq.q: Can visitors park all day on the streets below Bert Flinn Park?
faq.a: No. The City reminds park drivers that a vehicle may not be parked adjacent to another person's residential property for more than three hours between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., Monday to Friday, under Bylaw No. 1528 — a rule that affects the Heritage Mountain Boulevard and David Avenue trailhead streets.

faq.q: Is wildlife a real issue on the upper streets?
faq.a: Yes, on the City's own record. The City posted a notice after the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service received reports of an encounter with two cougars, an adult and a young cougar, in the Bert Flinn Park area, and directs sightings in urban areas to the Report All Poachers and Polluters line at 1-877-952-7277.

faq.q: Does one bus route cross the whole neighbourhood?
faq.a: Yes — route 182, Moody Centre Station/Belcarra, loops through Heritage Mountain on Heritage Mountain Boulevard, Ravine Drive and Turner Creek Drive, then continues via David Avenue and Aspenwood Drive into Anmore and Belcarra, so the same bus serves both the school-run streets and the inlet villages.

faq.q: What did houses in Heritage Mountain sell for?
faq.a: 19 houses sold in Heritage Mountain between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,750,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Heritage Mountain?
faq.a: The median was 14 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (11% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
